title: Collections and a Small Progress Tracker
summary: Lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets model different relationships. This lesson applies their trade-offs in a small progress-tracker project and introduces safe decomposition.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the Python behavior taught in Collections and a Small Progress Tracker
Test the behavior with a small observable program
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Choose a collection according to the operations the program needs. Lists preserve order and allow repeated values; tuples represent fixed-position records; dictionaries map unique keys to values; sets keep unique hashable members and provide efficient membership tests. Iterating over a dictionary yields keys, while `.items()` yields key-value pairs. Access with `mapping[key]` raises `KeyError` when absent; `.get(key, default)` expresses an expected fallback. Do not modify a list or dictionary structurally while iterating over the same view—build a new result or iterate over a copy. A useful small program separates input, domain calculation, and output formatting so each part can be tested.
keyPoints: Choose a collection according to the operations the program needs.

aliasing the same list means mutations are visible through both names

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Copy the example into a new `.py` file.
2. Predict every printed value and type.
3. Run it and compare evidence with the prediction.
4. Change one input or condition.
5. Record why the output changed.
6. Add an assertion that protects the intended behavior.
